evals.prompt: Create a standalone English TikZ figure for a synthetic two-pass scheduling algorithm. Both passes contain six functional tiers: eligibility check, request selection, tree refinement, resource/effort update, success sampling, completion/queue update. Pass A uses planned budgets; Pass B uses residual resources. Include the display formula T^* = argmax_{T in F_i(R)} [sum_{e in E_T} log p_e / (1 + c_e)] in the refinement nodes, and three explicit state-update lines in the resource nodes. Each sampling failure returns to its own eligibility check; each completion also returns there to select the next request. Exhausted budgets transfer A to B with a long label; exhausted residual resources lead to a global End-of-slot update below both panels. Deliver editable source, PDF and a PNG preview. Use the loaded skill and finish the requested work.
evals.expected_output: A complete compiled and visually inspected two-pass diagram preserving all stages and branches, with readable math, loopback labels, card bounds and global termination.

assertions.text: Both passes preserve the six supplied tiers, all return/transfer/exit edges and the global termination.
Measured node heights leave at least 14pt vertical clearance; display math and state updates do not overlap.
Parallel return labels are sloped and staggered; long transition and exit labels fit reserved corridors without cutting borders or adjacent wires.
Both cards contain all local nodes, headers and return labels; shared termination is below both with at least 20pt clearance.
Consumer compiles, renders, opens the actual preview, checks all five visual criteria, and rerenders any correction.

evals.prompt: Create an English SVG comparing two horizontal researcher-agent workflows. Each row has three cards: Researcher, Agent, Review. Researcher and Agent exchange feedback; Agent sends results to Review. Place the short labels Feedback and Results above their connector stems. Keep the figure readable in grayscale. Deliver editable SVG and an inspected PNG preview.
evals.expected_output: Aligned paired rows with correct arrow direction and off-stem labels; complex loopback geometry is not imposed on a simple flow.

assertions.text: Feedback is bidirectional and results are unidirectional.
Labels sit above continuous connector stems and do not touch card borders.
Consumer renders and opens the PNG, checks fit and grayscale readability, and preserves editable source.

evals.prompt: Provide a short handoff for a TikZ draft after discovering that this runtime has neither a TeX renderer nor an image viewer. No renderer or viewer can be installed in this task. Explain the actual verification status and give reproducible next steps; do not generate an artifact or run tools for this scenario.
evals.expected_output: Explicitly unverified visual status, source preserved, portable compile/render/open-image checks for a capable runtime, no invented QA pass.

assertions.text: Handoff states compilation and visual inspection remain unverified and does not claim the figure is complete or visually checked.
Next steps use available-tool discovery rather than a hardcoded Homebrew path and include opening the rendered image and the five visual checks.

evals.prompt: Plan a short English research deck from a source ledger with one trust boundary, one matched numerical comparison, one equation, and three short limitations. Give each content slide a visual decision, purpose and source or a reason for text-only. Do not invent data or add icons as decoration. Preserve the exact visible idea phrases in the plan and deck.
evals.expected_output: A slide-plan.json with meaningful diagram/chart/equation choices, justified text-only limitations, and source-backed idea wording that can be displayed at projection size.

assertions.text: Every new content slide has a visual type with source-backed purpose, or none with a concrete reason.
The trust boundary is a diagram and the numeric comparison is a chart from source values; the equation and caveats do not gain decorative icons.
Short source-faithful ideas appear verbatim in the visible deck and pass the unchanged check-deck contract.

evals.prompt: A source-backed deck would benefit from one Tabler icon naming a package. Select one icon from a pinned official release over HTTPS, preserve the license, create an auditable asset record, sanitize its SVG before local PNG rendering, and show any required credit in the exported PDF. Do not download an icon library or use a latest URL.
evals.expected_output: Only the selected asset is cached; visual-ledger.json records its release, URL, creator, license, changes, usage and hashes; sanitized SVG and PNG are retained and visually checked.

assertions.text: The asset URL identifies a concrete Tabler release and records MIT copyright/license information.
Raw SVG is never inserted or rendered first; active/external content is rejected, sanitized SVG is rasterized to PNG, and the result is inspected.
The selected asset has complete per-file provenance, SHA-256, slide mapping and visible PDF credit when required.

evals.prompt: Review a deck plan with an editable vector process slide, a native equation slide, and two consecutive content slides containing short limitations. The vector slide has no embedded bitmap. Run visual-plan review without adding an icon quota or changing the existing check-deck JSON output.
evals.expected_output: The vector diagram and equation remain valid visual decisions; text-only choices get non-blocking review warnings; no bitmap-presence test or hard icon quota is used.

assertions.text: A vector diagram is not called text-only merely because the PPTX contains no p:pic.
Justified consecutive text-only slides produce review warnings with exit 0, not a demand for filler icons.
check-deck.py retains its default JSON keys ok, slide_count and errors, with no new warnings field.
